**Most projects don't have one CDE. They have several, and the real work is moving files between them.** In Episode 4 of How to survive as a BIM Manager, Akos Hamar, Plannerly's COO, shows three ways to let files move themselves with your plan in the middle: Auto-Publish files an approved document in the client's SharePoint, Auto-Collect turns files dropped in the design team's Dropbox into filled requests and moving charts, and Auto-Route passes a reviewed drawing on to the contractor's Autodesk Forma. Each one is set up once in CDE Connect, then left to run.

**Good to know - watch in your language.** On YouTube, open the gear icon in the player. Subtitles/CC has Auto-translate, and Audio track has an auto-dubbed voice where one is available.

## What is a CDE, and why do projects end up with several?

A common data environment (CDE) is the agreed place where a project's information is collected, managed and shared. The ISO 19650 idea behind it is simple: you should always be able to find the latest version of the right file, from one source of truth.

That can work with several CDEs, as long as everyone knows which one to go to for which file, approval or certificate. In practice each company brings its own. With maybe 20 companies on a project, getting them all into one tool is a holy grail: some won't, and some can't, because of their IT rules or their contract.

## Why is it so hard to find the latest file?

- **The same file has a different status in every place.** One drawing can be S2 here, Approved there and FINAL\_v3 over there. So which one is the latest?
- **There's an eighth CDE: somebody's desktop.** "It's on my laptop. I'm on holiday until the 14th."
- **You become the courier.** Download, upload, rename, email, zip, thumb drive, in the post. Each tool works fine on its own. The trouble is in between.
- **The tracker can't keep up.** A tracker updated by hand is out of date as soon as the next file is issued.
- **Nobody has a receipt.** There's no agreed way to record what was sent and received. DOCie, an industry effort to agree how documents get exchanged, is the subject of a later webinar on 17 December.

## What are the three ways to deal with it?

| Way | What it means | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1\. Make everyone use one CDE | One tool for every company on the project | IT says no, the contract says no, and the meeting is adjourned |
| 2\. Manage the gaps | Syncs to set up, files moved by hand, workflows written down | Each tool works, you become the courier, and the tracker still falls behind |
| 3\. Automate it | Put your plan in the middle | Every team keeps its CDE, files move on a rule, and the plan checks them off |

Adding another CDE only adds complexity, so nobody is asked to move. Each team keeps what it uses today, and CDE Connect keeps them in step.

## What is CDE Connect?

CDE Connect is where you link a Plannerly project to another team's CDE. Choose the CDE, sign in, say whether files go out or come in, preview the automation and turn it on. The episode shows three automations:

| Automation | What it does | In the demo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auto-Publish - send it out | Publish it here, and it lands there | An approved document goes to the client's SharePoint |
| Auto-Collect - bring it in | Delivered there, filled here | Files in the design team's Dropbox fill their requests |
| Auto-Route - pass it on | Approved here, passed on | A reviewed drawing goes on to the contractor's Autodesk Forma |

For the whole job, step by step, see [how to connect your CDE](https://plannerly.com/use-cases/cde-connect/).

## How do you publish an approved document to a client's SharePoint automatically?

This demo picks up the project from [Episode 3](https://plannerly.com/live/surviving-information-requirements/), where AI drafted a pre-appointment execution plan from the client's EIR. The team has agreed it, and the client expects the appointment document in their SharePoint.

1. **Connect the client's SharePoint.** On the project dashboard, open CDE Connect, choose SharePoint and choose to send files.
2. **Pick the folder.** Find the client's project and the folder they look in. Here, that's Contracts.
3. **Set the condition.** Not every file should go out. The rule here sends only the document the team agreed, once it's approved.
4. **Preview, then turn it on.** The preview is empty at this point, because no file meets the condition yet.
5. **Create the document.** Export Docs and Scope into one PDF: the pre-appointment execution plan, the responsibility matrix and a cover page. The table of contents, headers and footers come with it, and it lands in File Manager.
6. **Request signatures.** Ask the team to sign from the Signatures column, then sign it yourself.
7. **Let it go.** Once everyone has signed, the status moves to Approved by itself and the document is published to SharePoint. If you can't wait, Check now runs the automation straight away.

Nobody attached anything and nobody uploaded anything. Signing is quick too, because nobody is seeing the document for the first time: as Clive Jordan, Plannerly's co-founder, pointed out, Bharathi Balu, Plannerly's Information Management Lead, had been part of it all the way through.

## How do files in someone else's Dropbox fill your MIDP?

This demo uses the MIDP from [Episode 1](https://youtu.be/HIboRq0w7tA): a list of expected drawings pasted into File Manager and turned into a scope. Every file shows as Requested at version 0, and the small charts in Scope are still amber. The architect keeps their files in Dropbox and has no reason to change.

1. **Link the Dropbox.** In CDE Connect, choose Dropbox, choose to collect files and sign in to the account.
2. **Pick the source folder.** It doesn't have to be tidy. Here everything sits in the root folder, and you can include subfolders too.
3. **Set default metadata.** Not every CDE holds metadata the way Plannerly does, so set defaults here, such as the author.
4. **Preview, then turn it on.**
5. **Watch the files arrive.** Each one shows Dropbox as its source, its status moves from Requested to Delivered and its version becomes 1.
6. **Check the charts.** The charts in Scope and in the project show what has arrived and what's still to come, and you can start reviewing straight away.

## Can progress reports send themselves?

Yes. The same charts can sit in a document, so a report takes no time to build. The one in the demo is short: delivery status and file planning readiness. Akos set it to go to the team every two weeks on a Thursday, with a second rule that sends each new version to the reports folder in Autodesk Forma. He created version 2, and it appeared there, matching Plannerly.

## How do approved drawings reach the contractor's Autodesk Forma?

Auto-Route puts the pieces together. Files come in, you review them, and the ones that pass your quality gate go on to the next team, in the CDE that team already uses.

1. **Choose your quality gate.** Akos used the suitability column: a drawing at S4 is ready for the contractor.
2. **Connect Autodesk Forma.** In CDE Connect, choose Autodesk Forma and choose to publish, then find the project and the folder. Here, that's approved drawings.
3. **Set the condition.** Suitability is S4. Preview it and turn it on.
4. **Review, then change the status.** Set a delivered drawing to S4 and it's published on the spot.
5. **Check Autodesk Forma.** The approved drawings appear in the contractor's folder.

To see the same files together in Plannerly, use File views. A favorite called S4 filters to those files, and SmartFolders sort files into folders from their metadata automatically.

For Autodesk, a company can also connect through a Secure Service Account rather than one person's sign-in, then add a connection project by project.

## What happens to file names when files come in?

Plannerly names each file to the project's file naming standard, whatever it was called in the architect's Dropbox. You keep both names: what they called it in their own system, and what you call it in Plannerly. Reports going out to Autodesk Forma carry the project's names as well.

2. **Click your CDE** and sign in.
3. **Choose Auto-Publish or Auto-Collect,** preview, then turn it on.

## Questions about working across several CDEs

What is a CDE?

A common data environment (CDE) is the agreed place where a project's information is collected, managed and shared. Under ISO 19650 the idea is that you can always find the latest version of the right file. A CDE is a tool and a way of working, which is why one project can end up with several.

How do I keep several CDEs in step?

Put your plan in the middle. Each team keeps the CDE it already uses, and CDE Connect links them to one Plannerly project. Auto-Publish sends files out, Auto-Collect brings them in and Auto-Route passes them on, so nobody has to be the courier. [Watch all three in the replay](https://plannerly.com/live/surviving-the-cdes/#replay).

How do I send an approved document to my client's SharePoint automatically?

Open CDE Connect, choose SharePoint and choose to send files. Pick the client's folder, set the condition, for example that the document is approved, preview it and turn it on. When everyone has signed, the document moves to Approved and is published to that folder.

How can files in a designer's Dropbox fill my MIDP?

Open CDE Connect, choose Dropbox and choose to collect files from the folder the designers already use. As files arrive they fill their requests, the delivery status moves from Requested to Delivered, and the charts update. The designers don't change a thing.

How do approved drawings get to the contractor's Autodesk Forma?

Set up an automation in CDE Connect that publishes to the contractor's folder, with a condition such as suitability S4. When you set a reviewed drawing to S4, it goes straight on to Autodesk Forma.

Which CDEs does CDE Connect work with?

CDE Connect lists Autodesk Forma (including ACC, Autodesk Docs and BIM 360), Procore, Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft OneDrive for Business, Dropbox and Box. To try new connectors early, join the beta testing community: sign in to Plannerly (or [sign up free](https://app.plannerly.com/sign-up)), open Support and type "add me".

Does a file keep its original name when Plannerly renames it?

Yes. You keep both names: what the team called it in their own system, and the name it gets in Plannerly from your file naming standard.

How do I stop files looping back and forth during a two-way sync?

Set the two directions up separately: one automation for what goes out, and another for what you collect on the way in. If you have a specific case, talk to us and we'll go through it.

Can I organize file requirements by discipline or floor?

Yes. Use metadata such as discipline, floor or stage. File Manager's tree view and SmartFolders then sort and filter your files from that metadata automatically.

What is DOCie?

DOCie is an industry effort to agree how documents get exchanged, so there's a receipt for what was sent and received. We'll cover it in a later webinar on 17 December.

Can I try CDE Connect for free?

Yes. File Manager features are free, and you can try the integrations. [Start with a free account](https://app.plannerly.com/sign-up), no card needed.
